(require 'yeah-tools)

(defgroup yeah-bridge nil
  "The Yeah emacsclient bridge."
  :group 'yeah)

(defcustom yeah-bridge-program "emacsclient"
  "Program used to reach the attached Emacs.

executable found on `exec-path' or the path of an executable file."
  :type 'string
  :group 'yeah-bridge)

(defcustom yeah-bridge-server nil
  "Name of the Emacs server the bridge connects to.
When nil, `emacsclient' connects to the default server.  A service
placement reaches a specific attached Emacs, so the name is a
capability: the operator names which Emacs the bridge may reach."
  :type '(choice (const nil) string)
  :group 'yeah-bridge)

(defconst yeah-bridge--timeout 2
  "Seconds a bridge call may take before its process is killed.")

(defconst yeah-bridge--probe "t"
  "Expression evaluated to find out whether the attached Emacs answers.")

(defun yeah-bridge--program-path ()
  "Return the path of the executable bridge program, or nil.
The program is not found when `yeah-bridge-program' is empty or
names a file that cannot be executed."
  (let ((program yeah-bridge-program))
    (and (stringp program)
         (> (length program) 0)
         (executable-find program))))

(defun yeah-bridge--trim (text)
  "Return TEXT without its trailing newlines."
  (let* ((text (or text ""))
         (end (length text)))
    (while (and (> end 0)
                (memq (aref text (1- end)) '(?\n ?\r)))
      (setq end (1- end)))
    (substring text 0 end)))

(defun yeah-bridge--stderr-text (buffer)
  "Return the text collected in the stderr BUFFER."
  (with-current-buffer buffer

(defun yeah-bridge--wait (process timeout)
  "Wait for PROCESS to exit, but no longer than TIMEOUT seconds.

  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) timeout)))

    (not (process-live-p process))))

  "Run PATH with ARGS and collect what it printed.

;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The bridge collects what the attached Emacs printed with a process
;; filter.  A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the filter:
;; the answer was then lost and the bridge reported success with an empty
;; output — the person saw an empty buffer that the server had never
;; emptied.  This check reads the same live buffer many times through the
;; bridge and requires that no answer is ever empty.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'yeah-bridge)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the server.")

(defvar yeah-check--emacsclient
  (let* ((dir (file-name-directory yeah-check--emacs))
         (candidate (expand-file-name "emacsclient" dir)))
    (or (and (file-executable-p candidate) candidate)
        (executable-find "emacsclient")
        candidate))
  "The emacsclient program that reaches the server.")

(defvar yeah-check--reads 120
  "How many times the check reads the buffer through the bridge.
Losing an answer is a race between the exit of the child process and the
delivery of its last chunk, so it shows up under load: the check keeps a
thread spinning to make the parent late, and reads often enough that the
loss is certain without the fix.")

(defvar yeah-check--load-thread nil
  "The thread that keeps the parent late, so the race can happen.")

(let ((failures nil)
      (name (format "yeah-bridge-keep-%d" (random 1000000)))
      (empty 0))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        (make-process
         :name "yeah-bridge-keep-server"
         :command (list yeah-check--emacs
                        (concat "--daemon=" name)
                        "--eval"
                        "(with-current-buffer (get-buffer-create \"*yeah-live*\") (insert \"live text\"))")
         :connection-type 'pipe
         :noquery t)
        ;; wait for the server
        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) 8)))
          (while (and (< (float-time) deadline)
                      (not (zerop (with-temp-buffer
                                    (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil
                                                  "-s" name "--eval" "t")))))
            (accept-process-output nil 0.1)))
        ;; a spinning thread makes the parent slow, which is when the
        ;; answer of the child is lost
        (setq yeah-check--load-thread
              (make-thread
               (lambda ()
                 (let ((counter 0))
                   (while (< counter 100000000)
                     (setq counter (1+ counter)))))))
        (dotimes (_ yeah-check--reads)
          (let ((text (condition-case err
                         (let ((yeah-bridge-program yeah-check--emacsclient)
                               (yeah-bridge-server name))
                           (yeah-bridge-buffer-read "*yeah-live*"))
                       (error (format "ERROR: %S" err)))))
            (when (or (null text) (equal text ""))
              (setq empty (1+ empty)))))
        (when (> empty 0)
          (push (format "the bridge lost the answer %d times out of %d"
                        empty yeah-check--reads)
                failures)))
    (when yeah-check--load-thread
      (ignore-errors (thread-signal yeah-check--load-thread 'quit)))
    (ignore-errors
      (with-temp-buffer
        (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil "-s" name "--eval" "(kill-emacs)"))))
    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message "bridge-keep: %s" failure))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

# AGENTS.md — the entry point to this repository

> **Yeah** means **Yeah, Emacs Agent Harness**: a recursive acronym, the
> **Y** is the Y-combinator. The harness itself is
> Emacs Lisp; Emacs is not merely a client to an external agent. The model is
> reached through gptel, effects go through the tool registry and permission
> system, and session history is append-only JSONL.
>
> The long-term Y metaphor means bounded recursive delegation, runtime
> self-inspection and a fixed point where Yeah can develop and verify Yeah.
> These are goals, not assertions about today's prototype.
>
> This repository is governed by **math-coding v5**: `spec.json` holds the
> standing specification (`schema_version: 5`) and the claims, `waves/*.json`
> holds the historical work units, and evidence comes from checks bound by
> `mathc run`.  Version 4 is frozen and archived at `waves/spec-v4.json`;
> its evidence is not current.
> `docs/PLAN.md` defines the current target sequence; do not mistake an old
> wave number or a green module row for a working end-to-end feature.

## Read first, in this order

1. `README.md` — actual current status and explicit limitations.
2. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — the normative target: purpose, ten decisions,
   contracts, security, placements and non-goals.
3. `docs/PLAN.md` — the detailed eight-stage execution plan and release gates.
4. `docs/ENGINEERING.md` — binding dependency, infrastructure, library,
   process, security, testing and packaging practices.
5. `spec.json` — the standing machine-checked specification.
6. `waves/*.json` — existing math-coding units, with intent, check, promise
   and objection.
7. `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md` — kernel Elisp conventions; §11 is the trap log.
8. `lib/yeah-*.el` — the implementation, one feature per file.

If two sources contradict each other, report the contradiction in the open
work item. Never resolve it by silently making documentation more optimistic.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The bridge collects what the attached Emacs printed with a process
;; filter.  A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the filter:
;; the answer was then lost and the bridge reported success with an empty
;; output — the person saw an empty buffer that the server had never
;; emptied.  This check reads the same live buffer many times through the
;; bridge and requires that no answer is ever empty.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'yeah-bridge)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the server.")

(defvar yeah-check--emacsclient
  (let* ((dir (file-name-directory yeah-check--emacs))
         (candidate (expand-file-name "emacsclient" dir)))
    (or (and (file-executable-p candidate) candidate)
        (executable-find "emacsclient")
        candidate))
  "The emacsclient program that reaches the server.")

(defvar yeah-check--reads 120
  "How many times the check reads the buffer through the bridge.
Losing an answer is a race between the exit of the child process and the
delivery of its last chunk, so it shows up under load: the check keeps a
thread spinning to make the parent late, and reads often enough that the
loss is certain without the fix.")

(defvar yeah-check--load-thread nil
  "The thread that keeps the parent late, so the race can happen.")

(let ((failures nil)
      (name (format "yeah-bridge-keep-%d" (random 1000000)))
      (empty 0))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        (make-process
         :name "yeah-bridge-keep-server"
         :command (list yeah-check--emacs
                        (concat "--daemon=" name)
                        "--eval"
                        "(with-current-buffer (get-buffer-create \"*yeah-live*\") (insert \"live text\"))")
         :connection-type 'pipe
         :noquery t)
        ;; wait for the server
        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) 8)))
          (while (and (< (float-time) deadline)
                      (not (zerop (with-temp-buffer
                                    (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil
                                                  "-s" name "--eval" "t")))))
            (accept-process-output nil 0.1)))
        ;; a spinning thread makes the parent slow, which is when the
        ;; answer of the child is lost
        (setq yeah-check--load-thread
              (make-thread
               (lambda ()
                 (let ((counter 0))
                   (while (< counter 100000000)
                     (setq counter (1+ counter)))))))
        (dotimes (_ yeah-check--reads)
          (let ((text (condition-case err
                         (let ((yeah-bridge-program yeah-check--emacsclient)
                               (yeah-bridge-server name))
                           (yeah-bridge-buffer-read "*yeah-live*"))
                       (error (format "ERROR: %S" err)))))
            (when (or (null text) (equal text ""))
              (setq empty (1+ empty)))))
        (when (> empty 0)
          (push (format "the bridge lost the answer %d times out of %d"
                        empty yeah-check--reads)
                failures)))
    (when yeah-check--load-thread
      (ignore-errors (thread-signal yeah-check--load-thread 'quit)))
    (ignore-errors
      (with-temp-buffer
        (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil "-s" name "--eval" "(kill-emacs)"))))
    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message "bridge-keep: %s" failure))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

### 18.1 Wave 41 — the verifier of the bridge decides the race by construction

**The defect.**  One verifier of the standing specification is a race.  The
check of `bridge-keeps-the-answer` reads the buffer of an attached Emacs a
hundred and twenty times while a thread keeps the parent late, and it fails
only when the answer is really lost.  Six runs of the evidence on 2026-11-16:
five bit, one did not — the control reached the subject, the verifier after
the control still passed, the claim came out `inconclusive`, and the map came
out `unknown`.  The code was not the cause of that verdict; the evidence was.

**Why this wave is first.**  Every other wave of this plan ends with a run
of the method, and a run whose verdict depends on a race may say `unknown`
for a reason that has nothing to do with the code it names.  A map that says
`unknown` because of a race cannot be read.

**What changes.**  The check stops racing the subject and starts commanding
it: the loss of the answer becomes a condition that the check arranges — a
barrier the parent waits for, a hook the check owns — so that the same
input gives the same verdict every time.  The control of the claim becomes
the same arrangement with one step removed, and the check must then fail by
its own assertion.

**The claims.**
- `bridge-keeps-the-answer` — the existing claim, re-bound with a control

- `the-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction` — a new claim: the
  check of the bridge gives the same verdict on ten consecutive runs of the

**The defect.**  Two defects of one life cycle.  The process of the ACP

(require 'yeah-tools)

(defgroup yeah-bridge nil
  "The Yeah emacsclient bridge."
  :group 'yeah)

(defcustom yeah-bridge-program "emacsclient"
  "Program used to reach the attached Emacs.

executable found on `exec-path' or the path of an executable file."
  :type 'string
  :group 'yeah-bridge)

(defcustom yeah-bridge-server nil
  "Name of the Emacs server the bridge connects to.

placement reaches a specific attached Emacs, so the name is a
capability: the operator names which Emacs the bridge may reach."
  :type '(choice (const nil) string)
  :group 'yeah-bridge)

(defconst yeah-bridge--timeout 2
  "Seconds a bridge call may take before its process is killed.")

(defconst yeah-bridge--probe "t"
  "Expression evaluated to find out whether the attached Emacs answers.")

(defun yeah-bridge--program-path ()
  "Return the path of the executable bridge program, or nil.
The program is not found when `yeah-bridge-program' is empty or
names a file that cannot be executed."
  (let ((program yeah-bridge-program))
    (and (stringp program)
         (> (length program) 0)
         (executable-find program))))

(defun yeah-bridge--trim (text)
  "Return TEXT without its trailing newlines."
  (let* ((text (or text ""))
         (end (length text)))
    (while (and (> end 0)
                (memq (aref text (1- end)) '(?\n ?\r)))
      (setq end (1- end)))
    (substring text 0 end)))

(defun yeah-bridge--stderr-text (buffer)
  "Return the text collected in the stderr BUFFER."
  (with-current-buffer buffer
    (buffer-string)))

(defun yeah-bridge--wait (process timeout)
  "Wait for PROCESS to exit, but no longer than TIMEOUT seconds.
Return non-nil when the process exited in time."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) timeout)))
    (while (and (process-live-p process)
                (< (float-time) deadline))
      (accept-process-output process 0.05))
    (not (process-live-p process))))

(defun yeah-bridge--run-program (path args timeout)
  "Run PATH with ARGS and collect what it printed.
Return a plist with the keys `:ok', `:status', `:output' and

  (let ((output "")
        (stderr-buffer (generate-new-buffer " *yeah-bridge stderr*"))
        (process nil))

        (condition-case err
            (progn
              (setq process (make-process
                             :name "yeah-bridge"
                             :command (cons path args)
                             :connection-type 'pipe
                             :noquery t
                             :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)
                             :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                                       (setq output (concat output chunk)))
                             :stderr stderr-buffer))

# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0

#   help                  — this text
#

#   0 — pass       (Green)

#

  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then

    return 0

  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"
    return 0

(require 'yeah-bridge)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))

(defvar yeah-check--emacsclient
  (let* ((dir (file-name-directory yeah-check--emacs))
         (candidate (expand-file-name "emacsclient" dir)))
    (or (and (file-executable-p candidate) candidate)
        (executable-find "emacsclient")
        candidate))
  "The emacsclient program that reaches the server.")

(defvar yeah-check--reads 120

delivery of its last chunk, so it shows up under load: the check keeps a

loss is certain without the fix.")

      (empty 0))

         :name "yeah-bridge-keep-server"
         :command (list yeah-check--emacs
                        (concat "--daemon=" name)
                        "--eval"
                        "(with-current-buffer (get-buffer-create \"*yeah-live*\") (insert \"live text\"))")
         :connection-type 'pipe
         :noquery t)

                         (let ((yeah-bridge-program yeah-check--emacsclient)

                           (yeah-bridge-buffer-read "*yeah-live*"))
                       (error (format "ERROR: %S" err)))))

;;; yeah-bridge.el --- the emacsclient bridge -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify
;; it under the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; An explicit, permissioned bridge to the buffers of an attached
;; Emacs, reached through `emacsclient'.  The bridge is a capability
;; and not a convenience: the two tools carry their own names, so
;; the permission system can approve `bridge__eval' and
;; `bridge__buffer_read' separately, and nothing enters the tool
;; registry until the operator asks for it with `yeah-bridge-register'.
;;
;; The program is started with `make-process' -- never through a
;; shell -- and every call is bounded by a short timeout, so a busy
;; or absent server cannot hang the agent.

;;; Code:

(require 'yeah-tools)

(defgroup yeah-bridge nil
  "The Yeah emacsclient bridge."
  :group 'yeah)

(defcustom yeah-bridge-program "emacsclient"
  "Program used to reach the attached Emacs.
The program is run directly, without a shell, so it must be an
executable found on `exec-path' or the path of an executable file."
  :type 'string
  :group 'yeah-bridge)

(defcustom yeah-bridge-server nil
  "Name of the Emacs server the bridge connects to.
When nil, `emacsclient' connects to the default server.  A service
placement reaches a specific attached Emacs, so the name is a
capability: the operator names which Emacs the bridge may reach."
  :type '(choice (const nil) string)
  :group 'yeah-bridge)

(defconst yeah-bridge--timeout 2
  "Seconds a bridge call may take before its process is killed.")

(defconst yeah-bridge--probe "t"
  "Expression evaluated to find out whether the attached Emacs answers.")

(defun yeah-bridge--program-path ()
  "Return the path of the executable bridge program, or nil.
The program is not found when `yeah-bridge-program' is empty or
names a file that cannot be executed."
  (let ((program yeah-bridge-program))
    (and (stringp program)
         (> (length program) 0)
         (executable-find program))))

(defun yeah-bridge--trim (text)
  "Return TEXT without its trailing newlines."
  (let* ((text (or text ""))
         (end (length text)))
    (while (and (> end 0)
                (memq (aref text (1- end)) '(?\n ?\r)))
      (setq end (1- end)))
    (substring text 0 end)))

(defun yeah-bridge--stderr-text (buffer)
  "Return the text collected in the stderr BUFFER."
  (with-current-buffer buffer
    (buffer-string)))

(defun yeah-bridge--wait (process timeout)
  "Wait for PROCESS to exit, but no longer than TIMEOUT seconds.
Return non-nil when the process exited in time."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) timeout)))
    (while (and (process-live-p process)
                (< (float-time) deadline))
      (accept-process-output process 0.05))
    (not (process-live-p process))))

(defun yeah-bridge--run-program (path args timeout)
  "Run PATH with ARGS and collect what it printed.
Return a plist with the keys `:ok', `:status', `:output' and
`:message'; see `yeah-bridge--run' for their meaning."
  (let ((output "")
        (stderr-buffer (generate-new-buffer " *yeah-bridge stderr*"))
        (process nil))
    (unwind-protect
        (condition-case err
            (progn
              (setq process (make-process
                             :name "yeah-bridge"
                             :command (cons path args)
                             :connection-type 'pipe
                             :noquery t
                             :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)
                             :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                                       (setq output (concat output chunk)))
                             :stderr stderr-buffer))
              (yeah-bridge--wait process timeout)
              (let ((timed-out (process-live-p process)))
                (when timed-out
                  (ignore-errors (kill-process process)))
                ;; A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the
                ;; filter: the answer of the attached Emacs is then lost
                ;; and the bridge answers with nothing.  Draining the
                ;; pending events after the exit — until the output stops
                ;; changing — gives the filter its last words.
                (let ((previous nil)
                      (drain-deadline (+ (float-time) 0.2)))
                  (while (and (< (float-time) drain-deadline)
                              (not (equal previous output)))
                    (setq previous output)
                    (accept-process-output nil 0.05)))
                (let ((status (unless timed-out (process-exit-status process))))
                  (list :ok (and (not timed-out) (eq status 0))
                        :status status
                        :output (yeah-bridge--trim output)
                        :message
                        (cond
                         (timed-out
                          (format "the attached Emacs did not answer within %s seconds"
                                  timeout))
                         ((not (eq status 0))
                          (let ((text (yeah-bridge--trim
                                       (yeah-bridge--stderr-text stderr-buffer))))
                            (if (> (length text) 0)
                                (format "the attached Emacs reported: %s" text)
                              "the attached Emacs reported an error")))
                         (t nil))))))
          (error
           (list :ok nil
                 :status nil
                 :output ""
                 :message (error-message-string err))))
      (when (and process (process-live-p process))
        (ignore-errors (delete-process process)))
      (when (buffer-live-p stderr-buffer)
        (kill-buffer stderr-buffer)))))

(defun yeah-bridge--run (args &optional timeout)
  "Run the bridge program with ARGS and collect what it printed.
ARGS is the list of command-line arguments without the program
itself.  TIMEOUT is the number of seconds the process may run.

Return a plist with the keys `:ok' (non-nil when the program
answered successfully), `:status' (the exit status), `:output' (the
standard output without trailing newlines) and `:message' (why the
call failed, or nil)."
  (let ((path (yeah-bridge--program-path))
        (args (append (when (and (stringp yeah-bridge-server)
                                 (> (length yeah-bridge-server) 0))
                        (list "-s" yeah-bridge-server))
                      args)))
    (if (null path)
        (list :ok nil
              :status nil
              :output ""
              :message (format "the bridge program %S is not executable"
                               yeah-bridge-program))
      (yeah-bridge--run-program path args (or timeout yeah-bridge--timeout)))))

(defun yeah-bridge-available-p ()
  "Return non-nil when the attached Emacs answers the bridge program.
The program must be executable and the attached Emacs must reply
within the bridge timeout.  This never signals: any failure means
that the bridge is unavailable."
  (condition-case nil
      (let ((result (yeah-bridge--run (list "--eval" yeah-bridge--probe))))
        (and (plist-get result :ok)
             (> (length (or (plist-get result :output) "")) 0)))
    (error nil)))

(defun yeah-bridge-eval (expression)
  "Evaluate EXPRESSION in the attached Emacs and return the printed result.
EXPRESSION is a string of Elisp code.  The result is the printed
value, as a string, without trailing newlines.

Signals `user-error' when the bridge is unavailable and when the
evaluation itself fails; the message says which of the two happened."
  (unless (stringp expression)
    (signal 'user-error
            (list (format "yeah-bridge-eval: expression must be a string, got %S"
                          (type-of expression)))))
  (let ((result (yeah-bridge--run (list "--eval" expression))))
    (if (plist-get result :ok)
        (plist-get result :output)
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-bridge-eval: %s"
                            (if (yeah-bridge-available-p)
                                (format "evaluation failed: %s"
                                        (or (plist-get result :message)
                                            "unknown error"))
                              "the bridge is unavailable")))))))

(defun yeah-bridge--decode (output)
  "Return the string OUTPUT holds, decoding its printed form.
`emacsclient --eval' prints the value of the evaluation: a string
arrives quoted, as its printed form.  When OUTPUT looks like a printed
string it is read back; anything else is returned unchanged."
  (if (and (stringp output)
           (> (length output) 1)
           (eq (aref output 0) ?\"))
      (condition-case nil (read output) (error output))
    output))

(defun yeah-bridge-buffer-read (name)
  "Return the text of the live buffer NAME of the attached Emacs.
NAME is the name of a buffer in the attached Emacs.  The result is
its text, as a string, without trailing newlines.

Signals `user-error' when the bridge is unavailable and when the
buffer cannot be read there; the message says which of the two
happened."
  (unless (stringp name)
    (signal 'user-error
            (list (format "yeah-bridge-buffer-read: name must be a string, got %S"
                          (type-of name)))))
  (let* ((expression
          (format (concat "(with-current-buffer %S "
                          "(buffer-substring-no-properties (point-min) (point-max)))")
                  name))
         (result (yeah-bridge--run (list "--eval" expression))))
    (if (plist-get result :ok)
        (yeah-bridge--decode (plist-get result :output))
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-bridge-buffer-read: %s"
                            (if (yeah-bridge-available-p)
                                (format "buffer %S could not be read: %s"
                                        name
                                        (or (plist-get result :message)
                                            "unknown error"))
                              "the bridge is unavailable")))))))

(defun yeah-bridge-tool-specs ()
  "Return the bridge tool specifications, in registration order."
  (list
   (list :name "bridge__eval"
         :description
         "Evaluate an Elisp expression in the attached Emacs and return the printed value."
         :input (list (list :name "expression" :type 'string))
         :handler #'yeah-bridge-eval)
   (list :name "bridge__buffer_read"
         :description
         "Return the contents of a live buffer of the attached Emacs."
         :input (list (list :name "name" :type 'string))
         :handler #'yeah-bridge-buffer-read)))

(defun yeah-bridge-register ()
  "Register the bridge tools in the tool registry and return them.
The registration is idempotent: a tool that is already registered is
kept as it is, so calling this twice does not raise an error.
The permission system matches the tool name as the action, so
`\"bridge__eval\"' and `\"bridge__buffer_read\"' are approved on
their own."
  (let ((specs (yeah-bridge-tool-specs)))
    (dolist (spec specs)
      (unless (yeah-tools-get (plist-get spec :name))
        (yeah-tools-register spec)))
    specs))

(provide 'yeah-bridge)

;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.

;; it under the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The service placement is the default of the product: `M-x yeah' opens it,
;; and the attached placement stays reachable by name (`yeah-attached') as the
;; development path and the fallback.
;;
;; The check asks the entry point twice: once when the service answers, and
;; once when the service cannot start.  The service must be asked first, and
;; the attached path must open ONLY when the service failed.  A silent
;; fallback would hide a broken service behind a working session, so the
;; fallback has to happen in the open.
;;
;; Exit codes: 0 — the entry point behaves; 1 — it does not.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'yeah)

(let ((failures nil)
      (service-calls 0)
      (attached-calls 0))
  ;; --- the service answers: it is the placement that opens
  (cl-letf (((symbol-function 'yeah-service)
             (lambda (&optional _name)
               (setq service-calls (1+ service-calls))))
            ((symbol-function 'yeah--open-attached)
             (lambda ()
               (setq attached-calls (1+ attached-calls)))))
    (yeah))
  (unless (= 1 service-calls)
    (push (format "the service was asked %d times, not once" service-calls)
          failures))
  (unless (= 0 attached-calls)
    (push (format "the attached placement opened %d times while the service answered"
                  attached-calls)
          failures))

  ;; --- the service cannot start: the attached path opens instead
  (setq service-calls 0
        attached-calls 0)
  (cl-letf (((symbol-function 'yeah-service)
             (lambda (&optional _name)
               (signal 'user-error "the service cannot start")))
            ((symbol-function 'yeah--open-attached)
             (lambda ()
               (setq attached-calls (1+ attached-calls)))))
    (let ((inhibit-message t))
      (yeah)))
  (unless (= 1 attached-calls)
    (push (format "the attached placement opened %d times after the service failed, not once"
                  attached-calls)
          failures))

  ;; --- the attached path is reachable by name
  (unless (fboundp 'yeah-attached)
    (push "there is no yeah-attached command" failures))
  (let ((attached-calls 0))
    (cl-letf (((symbol-function 'yeah--open-attached)
               (lambda ()
                 (setq attached-calls (1+ attached-calls)))))
      (yeah-attached))
    (unless (= 1 attached-calls)
      (push (format "yeah-attached opened the attached path %d times, not once"
                    attached-calls)
            failures)))
  (when failures
    (dolist (failure (reverse failures))
      (message "check-yeah-opens-the-service: %s" failure))
    (kill-emacs 1)))
